correctness.rationale: First-hit time finite by a positive-probability m-step success block. Independent type-refresh Poisson clocks yield exact from-empty and from-all transition probabilities. Strong Markov first-passage convolution yields the Laplace resolvent ratio and discrete PGF. Small-s expansion gives the subset mean, Karamata yields strict Schur-convexity since \(\log(1-e^{-tx})\) is strictly concave and \(\log(1+r e^{-tx})\) is convex. This covers \(p=0\), every finite \(m\ge 2\) and all strictly positive weights. A separate \(2^m\)-state rational checker validates 207 finite instances, without treating samples as proof.

value.rationale: Optimizing sampling effort is a natural, previously unresolved choice in the recent nonmonotone coupon-refresh model. The full finite first-hitting PGF and subset-sum mean identify the objective for arbitrary positive frequencies; strict Schur-convexity solves its allocation problem at every common positive loss rate and strictly quantifies improvement under balancing. It differs structurally from classical monotone coupon optimality, and supplies an analytically motivated exact finite result, not a routine parameter renaming.
